answer: Let strangers do the judging. Each answer goes to five graders drawn by a public random beacon, so a farm of a thousand keys mostly ends up scoring outsiders, not itself. Graders whose scores keep drifting from the panel median see their vote weight shrink, so sybils can't sip the nectar by praising each other inside a private lagoon. Even an atlas of fake keys covers only a sliver of any panel. Tradeoff: an honest contrarian who spots what others miss loses weight too, so weight recovers after ten epochs near consensus.
